findings.claim: The bundled command_race.xml defines 140 named RACE commands with typed fields and timeout values. These are SDK schemas, not captured PLYR exchanges.
The SDK schema distinguishes request types 0x5A and 0x5C. It distinguishes response types 0x5B and 0x5D. A decoder must retain these distinctions.

The command book defines storage program, erase, partition lookup, SHA256, integrity, commit, cancel, FOTA state, firmware version, and ROFS reads. These provide a concrete map for later update analysis.
Airoha symbols expose FOTA implementations for AB155x, AB1562, AB1568, and AB1585. The SDK contains validation and apply routines. This does not identify the chip used in PLYR.

Airoha strings identify FotaHeaderInfo and FotaParseError. A diagnostic rejects firmware bins smaller than 4k. Another diagnostic reports an unrecognized header type. Exact header fields and executable code paths remain unverified.
findings.status: artifact-confirmed strings; behavior inferred from diagnostics

findings.claim: BragiCore contains CryptoKitManager encrypt and decrypt functions and imports AES-GCM. mSDK exposes ChannelCipherContext and SessionAuthenticator functions for encryption and decryption. These names concern communications or library data. They do not establish firmware encryption.
RxBragi provides CRC16 and CRC8 routines. CRC routines detect changes in data. They are not evidence of firmware decryption.
The Airoha binary links CoreBluetooth and ExternalAccessory. These dependencies support further transport analysis, but they do not identify the transport selected for PLYR.
No THX or aux selector was established by the targeted symbol and string filters. App.framework was outside this batch. Absence from filtered results does not prove absence from the app.

The SDK names command 0x0A0C READ_NVKEY_RESP_NVID. Its request carries nvkey_id:uint16 followed by length:uint16. Therefore the documented SLYR bytes 02 10 e8 03 fit NVKEY 0x1002 and length 1000 if little-endian interpretation holds. This refines the earlier device-info label but does not prove the contents of NVKEY 0x1002 on PLYR.
findings.status: artifact-confirmed command name; cross-source interpretation inferred

limitations: No decompilation or live protocol test occurred.
The XML does not establish byte order by itself. Repository evidence may establish byte order for specific transports.
Symbols have Mach-O addresses. Strings have file offsets. These values are not interchangeable.
Some Swift symbols share addresses because compiler optimizations combine implementations.
The firmware container has not been parsed. No key was recovered.
No credentials or cryptographic key bytes were extracted.
Other bundled protocols, including Bragi and Jieli, must not be assumed to use the Airoha command book.
The broad SDK contains commands for many models. PLYR capability checks are still required.
